description:
FILED s473f (Opus, 2026-09-09), measured, with the prize counted.

A DIRHANDLE's payload is the `(index . names)` CONS, and a box holding a cons
is a LIST in PCL's model -- so a dirhandle answers as an ARRAY:

    opendir(my $fh, "/etc") or die;
    ref $fh          perl: GLOB     PCL: ARRAY
    "$fh"            perl: GLOB(0xâ¦)  PCL: "0 . .. .java .pwd.lock â¦"
                                       (the whole directory, joined)

t/op/readdir.t rows 52/54/56 (`is(ref $fh, 'GLOB')`) have always failed on it.
s473f's #1309 made `opendir($fh[0],â¦)` and `opendir($fh{abc},â¦)` INSTALL into
the element, and that turned rows 57-58 -- `isnt("$fh", "$fh[0]")` and
`isnt("$fh", "$fh{abc}")` -- from PASSING ON NOTHING (two of the three were
undef, so of course they differed) into honest failures: all three now hold
their own cons and all three stringify to the same joined listing.  The file
went 13/3 -> 11/5 and the snapshot carries that with this cause.

THE PRIZE IS +5 ROWS in that file alone (52, 54, 56, 57, 58), and the fix is
the #1308 rule applied to the third handle kind:

  * `%p-handle-payload-p` answers for a dirhandle cons as well, so `ref`/
    `reftype` say GLOB and the box counts as a glob REF.  It must be asked
    LAST and only for a CONS -- the predicate is on two HOT element unboxers.
  * `stringify-value` needs the matching arm BEFORE its list arm, or the word
    and the string disagree, which is exactly the bug #1308 fixed for streams.
  * The discriminator has to be "this cons is a REGISTERED dirhandle"
    (%p-dirhandle-path answers) rather than "this is a cons", because a cons
    is also PCL's list-backed pseudo-array.

MEASURE FIRST whether the gethash in the element unboxers costs anything
(tools/bench-exec.pl's arrhash / feread rows): s473f rejected a 4 ns test on
p-get-stream at -6.4 % on the io rows, and the same standard applies here.

The alternative -- give a dirhandle its own STRUCT instead of a bare cons --
is cleaner and removes the ambiguity for good, but it touches %p-resolve-dh,
%p-opendir-impl, *p-dirhandle-paths* and every reader; size it before choosing.
subject: A DIRHANDLE reads as an ARRAY: its `(index . names)` cons is a LIST in the box model, so ref() says ARRAY and "$dh" prints the whole directory (+5 rows in t/op/readdir.t)
